changes.baseline_text: And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.
changes.candidate_text: And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kind. And God saw that they were good.
changes.rationale: Propose singular 'their kind' in the final classification phrase: the Greek has singular kind with plural their, unlike the plural kinds in 1:21. The singular English is intelligible for a distributed class and preserves this source distinction. The three animal classes and repeated kind formulas remain. 'All' qualifies the creeping things here. 'Cattle' keeps the established broader traditional livestock term; its possible modern narrowing should be checked at read-aloud review. Plural 'they were good' reflects the plural evaluation.

changes.baseline_text: And God caused every tree that was beautiful to behold and good for food to spring up from the earth, with the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
changes.candidate_text: And God also caused every tree that was beautiful to behold and good for food to spring up from the earth, with the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
changes.rationale: The inherited wording accounts for the trees' visual beauty, food, life and knowledge, but leaves the source's eti unexpressed. Propose 'also caused' to preserve its additive force, consistent with 'also formed' in 2:19. The knowledge-tree construction is compressed into intelligible English without claiming its syntax has no difficulty. 'Knowledge' remains preferable here to adding moral autonomy or an explanation of the tree's power.

changes.baseline_text: And the Lord God fashioned the rib He had taken from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
changes.candidate_text: And the Lord God built the rib He had taken from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
changes.rationale: The source uses a building verb for the transformation of the taken rib into a woman. Propose 'built' in place of 'fashioned' to retain that concrete image and distinguish it from the earlier forming vocabulary. 'Built the rib ... into a woman' is unusual but intelligible English. Rib/side remains an unresolved lexical choice from 2:21; this proposal changes the verb only.

changes.baseline_text: For God knew that on the day you ate of it, your eyes would be opened, and you would be as gods, knowing good and evil.”
changes.candidate_text: For God knew that on the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be as gods, knowing good and evil.”
changes.rationale: The source has a past knowing verb followed by an eating condition and future eye-opening and becoming clauses. Propose present/future English within the serpent's direct speech so 'you ate ... would be' is not mistaken for an already completed meal. Preserve 'God knew' rather than silently changing that source tense. The plural gods remains, without deciding whether the comparison denotes deities or divine beings. No doctrinal explanation is inserted.

changes.baseline_text: And the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
changes.candidate_text: And the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings about their waists.
changes.rationale: The opening of both pairs of eyes, recognition of nakedness, sewing of fig leaves and making of coverings are present. Propose 'coverings about their waists' because the garment term is more specific than unqualified coverings and refers to something girded around the body. This is not an assertion about a precise garment pattern or its dimensions; the narrative image is simply made clearer.

changes.baseline_text: And God said, “Behold, Adam has become as one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he stretch forth his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever—”
changes.candidate_text: And God said, “Behold, Adam has become as one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he stretch forth his hand and take from the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever—”
changes.rationale: The becoming-like-one-of-us clause concerns knowing good and evil; the prevention clause then lists reaching, taking, eating and living forever. Propose deleting 'also' before 'from the tree of life': the source coordinates the actions with and, but does not separately mark this taking as 'also'. The unfinished-speech dash is an English presentation choice. Plural Us is retained without specifying its referent or resolving the speech's tone.

changes.baseline_text: And the Lord God saw that the wickedness of mankind had multiplied upon the earth, and that each one continually set his heart upon evil all his days.
changes.candidate_text: And the Lord God saw that the wickedness of mankind had multiplied upon the earth, and that each one intently devised evil in his heart every day.
changes.rationale: The source's adverb describes diligence or intentness; inherited continually blurs that with the separate all-days expression. Propose intently with every day, and keep the heart as the location of thought. English past tense fits the reported object of saw, while the Greek present describes habitual activity. This is a lexical-contextual proposal without a consulted specialist lexicon.

changes.baseline_text: Of all the winged birds according to their kind, all the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things upon the earth according to their kinds, two of each shall come to you, male and female, to be sustained with you.
changes.candidate_text: Of all the winged birds according to their kind, all the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things upon the earth according to their kind, two of each shall come to you, male and female, to be sustained with you.
changes.rationale: Unlike 6:19's command to bring, this clause says the creatures will enter to Noah. The final kind noun is singular with a plural possessive; propose their kind in place of their kinds to keep the source form consistent. Sustained represents the feeding purpose, and the male/female phrase remains.

changes.baseline_text: “And take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself. It shall be food for you and for them.”
changes.candidate_text: “And take for yourself some of every kind of food that you shall eat, and gather it to yourself. It shall be food for you and for them.”
changes.rationale: The source shifts from singular Noah's taking/gathering to plural you will eat. The inherited impersonal that is eaten hides that future addressee. Propose you shall eat while retaining natural number-neutral English you; note the plural explicitly here. Some of renders the partitive from without demanding every existing item of food be taken.

changes.baseline_text: two by two they entered the ark with Noah, male and female, as God had commanded him.
changes.candidate_text: two by two they came into the ark to Noah, male and female, as God had commanded him.
changes.rationale: The source says entered to Noah, whereas inherited with Noah can imply merely simultaneous accompaniment. Propose came to Noah in the ark-entry construction to make him the destination/person approached. Pairing and correspondence with God's command remain; this does not recalculate the sevens.

changes.baseline_text: entered the ark with Noah, two by two of all flesh in which is the breath of life.
changes.candidate_text: came into the ark to Noah, two by two of all flesh in which is the breath of life.
changes.rationale: As in 7:9, the source says to Noah, not merely with Noah. Propose came to Noah while retaining entry into the ark. Breath of life is a contextual rendering of the spirit/breath term and the two-by-two description remains. No animal kind is dropped from the preceding subject list.

changes.baseline_text: And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and covered all the high mountains beneath heaven.
changes.candidate_text: And the waters prevailed exceedingly, exceedingly upon the earth, and covered all the high mountains beneath heaven.
changes.rationale: The Greek intensifies with an adverb and related adverb together; the inherited one exceedingly compresses the deliberate repetition. Propose exceedingly, exceedingly to expose that emphasis in the literary candidate, with spoken cadence needing human review. All high mountains beneath heaven remains unchanged.

changes.baseline_text: And the waters steadily withdrew from the earth; after one hundred and fifty days the waters had receded and diminished.
changes.candidate_text: And the waters steadily withdrew from the earth; after one hundred and fifty days the waters continued to recede and diminish.
changes.rationale: The source repeats the recession verb and uses imperfect forms for receding and diminishing after 150 days. Inherited had receded and diminished can suggest completed recession by that point. Propose continued to recede and diminish after the stated interval, keeping the first steady withdrawal and the second repeated description.

changes.baseline_text: And all the wild beasts, all the cattle, every bird, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth came out of the ark according to their kinds.
changes.candidate_text: And all the wild beasts, all the cattle, every bird, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth came out of the ark according to their kind.
changes.rationale: All four animal groups exit the ark. The final Greek kind is singular with a plural possessive; propose their kind instead of their kinds, matching the same construction at 6:20. No claim is made that this grammatical category is identical with a modern biological species.

changes.baseline_text: And he drank of the wine and became drunk, and lay uncovered in his house.
changes.candidate_text: And he drank of the wine and became drunk, and was uncovered in his house.
changes.rationale: Drinking, drunkenness and uncoveredness are distinct. The source says house, so it is retained rather than substituted with tent from another textual form. Lay is supplied in the inherited reading though the Greek does not explicitly state posture; propose was uncovered to avoid adding that detail.

changes.baseline_text: And Noah awoke from his wine and knew what his younger son had done to him.
changes.candidate_text: And Noah became sober from his wine and knew what his younger son had done to him.
changes.rationale: The selected verb concerns recovering sobriety, not explicitly waking from sleep. Propose became sober instead of awoke to avoid importing sleep from the scene. Younger follows the comparative form; youngest remains a contextual possibility requiring kinship review, not an automatic replacement.

changes.baseline_text: He was a giant hunter before the Lord God; therefore it is said, “Like Nimrod, a giant hunter before the Lord.”
changes.candidate_text: He was a giant hunter before the Lord God; therefore they shall say, “Like Nimrod, a giant hunter before the Lord.”
changes.rationale: The first divine title is Lord God and the repeated saying has Lord alone. The reporting verb is future plural they will say, whereas inherited it is said changes tense and voice. A customary or gnomic future can justify the inherited present as a contextual rendering; the future active is therefore a proposal exposing the Greek form, not proof that the inherited tense was wrong. Before remains neutral between presence and a more adversarial interpretation.

changes.baseline_text: “Come, let Us go down and confound their language there, so that they may no longer understand one another’s speech.”
changes.candidate_text: “Come, let Us go down and confound their language there, so that they may not understand one another’s speech.”
changes.rationale: The source has a negative purpose clause without a separate no-longer expression. Propose may not understand instead of may no longer understand, preserving the mutual communication sense without an additional temporal adverb. The plural deliberation is retained; capital Us is inherited editorial styling, not identification of its participants.

changes.baseline_text: Therefore its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord confounded the languages of the whole earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
changes.candidate_text: Therefore its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord confounded the speech of the whole earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
changes.rationale: The source names the place by the translated meaning Confusion. Its plural lips is a speech metaphor and does not require multiple pre-existing languages; propose the collective speech instead of languages. Lord appears in the first explanation and Lord God in the second, preserved in the candidate. No automatic substitution of Babel or Babylon is made.

changes.baseline_text: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? And now, look, your wife is before you; take her and hurry away.”
changes.candidate_text: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’? And I took her as my wife. And now, look, your wife is before you; take her and hurry away.”
changes.rationale: Propose separating Pharaoh's question from the coordinated statement that he took Sara as wife. The source's simple and does not require the inherited so that, which may imply Abram intended that result. The visible wife, taking her and urgent departure remain.

changes.baseline_text: And he said to him, “Behold, I have regarded your face in this matter also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
changes.candidate_text: And he said to him, “Behold, I have shown you favour in this matter also: I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
changes.rationale: Propose shown you favour for the idiom literally honoring/regarding a face. The context grants Lot's request by sparing the named city; the colon carries that explanatory relation. The face image and literal alternative are retained in this record rather than requiring readers to decode the idiom unaided.

changes.baseline_text: And Abraham said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that they may be a witness to me that I have dug this well.”
changes.candidate_text: And Abraham said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from me, that they may be a witness to me that I have dug this well.”
changes.rationale: The seven ewe lambs are to be received 'from me' as witness that Abraham dug this well. The inherited 'from my hand' supplies an unexpressed body part; propose the direct 'from me' while retaining the purpose clause and singular well.

changes.baseline_text: “Now therefore come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and let it be a witness between me and you.” And he said to him, “Behold, no one is with us; see, God is witness between me and you.”
changes.candidate_text: “Now therefore come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and it shall be a witness between me and you.” And he said to him, “Behold, no one is with us; see, God is witness between me and you.”
changes.rationale: The first witness statement has a future form. Propose shall be to preserve that prospective wording, but a future can have directive force in a covenant setting, so inherited let it be is a defensible contextual rendering rather than an established error. The extra divine-witness speech belongs within this source-numbered unit, not a fabricated additional verse.

changes.baseline_text: “You shall be over my house, and all my people shall obey your mouth; only in the throne shall I be above you.”
changes.candidate_text: “You shall be over my house, and all my people shall obey your command; only in the throne shall I be above you.”
changes.rationale: Propose obey your command for the metonym obey at your mouth. Mouth expresses authoritative speech here; command makes it intelligible in English while the throne alone remains Pharaoh's exception. The literal image stays recorded as an alternative.

changes.baseline_text: And he said, “My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left; and if he should fall sick on the way which you go, you shall bring down my old age with sorrow into Hades.”
changes.candidate_text: And he said, “My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left; and he will fall sick on the way you go, and you shall bring down my old age with sorrow into Hades.”
changes.rationale: Propose restoring the future assertion: he will fall sick on the way. The Greek here has a future rather than the inherited if-clause; it expresses Jacob's feared prediction, not the narrator's certainty. Old age, sorrow and Hades remain.

changes.baseline_text: And Israel their father said to them, “If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry down gifts to the man, resin and honey, spices and stacte, terebinth nuts and nuts.
changes.candidate_text: And Israel their father said to them, “If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry down gifts to the man, resin and honey, incense and stacte, terebinth nuts and nuts.
changes.rationale: Propose incense rather than spices for the selected fumigation noun. Resin, honey, stacte, terebinth and nuts remain distinct; botanical identities and stacte's precise substance remain unresolved rather than replaced with familiar alternative plants.

changes.baseline_text: And he said to his daughters, “And where is he? Why have you left the man behind? Call him, therefore, that he may eat bread.”
changes.candidate_text: And he said to his daughters, “And where is he? Why have you left the man behind like this? Call him, therefore, that he may eat bread.”
changes.rationale: The father asks where the man is and why they left him in this manner, then commands an invitation so he may eat bread. Propose like this to represent the manner adverb lost in the inherited question. Bread remains the concrete food/meal expression, without inventing a larger feast.

changes.baseline_text: Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord with which He had sent him, and all the signs He had commanded him.
changes.candidate_text: Moses told Aaron all the words the Lord had sent, and all the signs He had commanded him.
changes.rationale: The relative pronoun after all the Lord's words is masculine accusative plural, matching words as what was sent. The inherited with which He had sent him introduces a personal object and instrumental relation not expressed here; propose words the Lord had sent, leaving the separate commanded-signs clause intact.

changes.baseline_text: Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the Lord for me, and let Him remove the frogs from me and my people. I will let them go so that they may sacrifice to the Lord.”
changes.candidate_text: Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the Lord for me, and let Him remove the frogs from me and my people. I will let the people go so that they may sacrifice to the Lord.”
changes.rationale: Pharaoh asks prayer for himself and removal from himself and his people, then promises to release the people. The inherited them can point back to Egyptians; restore the explicit the people to preserve the Greek switch to the captive people who will sacrifice.

changes.baseline_text: Do you still act against My people, refusing to let them go?
changes.candidate_text: Yet you still act against My people, refusing to let them go.
changes.rationale: The selected edition punctuates an accusation, with still and therefore/yet, rather than a question. Propose Yet you still act against My people, refusing to let them go. This follows editorial punctuation, not proof that a Greek indicative cannot be a rhetorical question, and is not a claim of a manuscript variant. The uncommon verb's precise oppression or interference nuance remains unresolved.

changes.baseline_text: And Pharaoh’s attendants said to him, “How long shall this be a hindrance to us? Let the men go, that they may serve their God. Or do you want to know that Egypt is destroyed?”
changes.candidate_text: And Pharaoh’s attendants said to him, “How long shall this be a hindrance to us? Let the people go, that they may serve their God. Or do you want to know that Egypt is destroyed?”
changes.rationale: The attendants call the situation a hindrance and urge release of the human group, using the general people/persons noun. Propose people instead of men here, preserving its distinction from the explicit male-only noun in 10:11; the final question about knowing Egypt's destruction remains unchanged.

changes.baseline_text: Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.
changes.candidate_text: Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take an animal from the flock for the ancestral households, one animal for each household.
changes.rationale: The tenth-day instruction apportions one animal by ancestral household and then by house. The flock-animal noun is broad enough to include the goat option expressly permitted in 12:5; propose animal from the flock rather than species-restrictive sheep, retaining the repeated one-per-house structure.

changes.baseline_text: If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the sheep.
changes.candidate_text: If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for an animal from the flock, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the animal.
changes.rationale: A small household combines with its nearest neighbour according to the number of persons and each one's sufficient portion. Use animal from the flock consistently with 12:3 and the sheep-or-goat alternatives in 12:5; the reckoning is by consumption capacity, not an invented fixed group size.

changes.baseline_text: Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
changes.candidate_text: Your animal from the flock shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
changes.rationale: The animal must be unblemished, male and one year old, and may be taken from lambs or young goats. Replace Your sheep with Your animal from the flock so the opening noun does not contradict the explicit goat category; retain and as the source's coordination of the available groups.

changes.baseline_text: Moses called the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, “Go and take a sheep for your families, and slaughter the Passover.
changes.candidate_text: Moses called the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, “Go and take an animal from the flock for your families, and slaughter the Passover.
changes.rationale: Moses gathers the entire elders' council and tells families to take the Passover animal. Propose animal from the flock instead of sheep, following the same inclusive noun and the lamb-or-young-goat eligibility of 12:5; slaughter remains the concrete ritual action.

changes.baseline_text: there on the surface of the wilderness was something fine, like white coriander, like frost on the ground.
changes.candidate_text: behold, on the surface of the wilderness was something fine, like white coriander, like frost on the ground.
changes.rationale: The publisher includes an attention marker; inherited there partly conveys its deictic presentation. Propose behold in place of there to expose that marker more explicitly in the unexpected sight, as a fidelity/register choice rather than proof that the inherited wording is erroneous. Both comparisons belong here, including white coriander, rather than being moved solely to 16:31.

changes.baseline_text: And the Lord said to Moses, “Come up to Me into the mountain, and remain there; and I will give you the tablets of stone, the law and the commandments which I have written to give them as law.”
changes.candidate_text: And the Lord said to Moses, “Come up to Me into the mountain, and remain there; and I will give you the tablets of stone, the law and the commandments which I have written to establish as law for them.”
changes.rationale: The dative them belongs with legislating for the people, whereas inherited give them as law makes them sound like a direct reference to the commandments and leaves the recipients implicit. Propose establish as law for them to represent the dative relation while keeping the written commands as understood object. The tablets, law and commandments remain; their exact appositional relation still needs syntax review.

changes.baseline_text: they shall wash their hands and feet with water. When they enter the Tent of Testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. This shall be a perpetual statute for him and his generations after him.”
changes.candidate_text: they shall wash their hands and feet with water. When they enter the Tent of Testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. This shall be a perpetual statute for them, for him and his generations after him.”
changes.rationale: The Greek repeats washing and death avoidance, then states the statute for them and for him and his generations. Propose restoring the omitted plural for them while retaining the subsequent singular shift.

changes.baseline_text: And from it he shall offer up an offering unto the Lord: the fat which covers the belly, and all the fat upon the belly,
changes.candidate_text: And upon it he shall offer up an offering unto the Lord: the fat which covers the belly, and all the fat upon the belly,
changes.rationale: Fat covering the belly and all fat on it are named again. Propose upon it for the opening prepositional phrase: the displayed Greek has epi, not apo. The preceding altar is a plausible referent for it, but the candidate leaves the pronoun unresolved rather than inserting altar. The selected preposition must not be silently assimilated to the from-phrases in 3:3 and 3:9.

changes.baseline_text: And if his hand cannot provide enough for a sheep, he shall bring unto the Lord for the sin which he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
changes.candidate_text: And if his hand cannot provide enough for an animal from the flock, he shall bring unto the Lord for the sin which he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
changes.rationale: The hand idiom expresses insufficient means. Propose animal from the flock instead of sheep because the preceding eligible offering explicitly includes a female goat. The two birds remain alternatives, with one for sin and one for whole burning.

changes.baseline_text: And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
changes.candidate_text: And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its paws shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
changes.rationale: Propose paws for hands in the quadruped context. LSJ cheir I.3 explicitly covers animal paws and cites this passage; the close stage preserves the inherited literal hands wording.

changes.baseline_text: And the Tent of Testimony and the camp of the Levites shall be raised in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they shall set out, each beside his neighbour according to command.
changes.candidate_text: And the Tent of Testimony and the camp of the Levites shall set out in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they shall set out, each beside his neighbour according to command.
changes.rationale: Propose shall set out for shall be raised: the tent and Levitical camp move among the marching camps, and the following clause explicitly compares camping with departure. The close draft retains shall be taken up.

changes.baseline_text: And their enrolment by their divisions was two thousand seven hundred fifty.
changes.candidate_text: And their enrolment by their divisions was two thousand two hundred fifty.
changes.rationale: Propose two thousand two hundred fifty in place of two thousand seven hundred fifty. The selected Greek explicitly reads dischilioi diakosioi pentekonta, or 2,250; the resulting disagreement with the chapter total is preserved for apparatus review.

changes.baseline_text: But if Thou do thus unto me, slay me outright, if I have found mercy with Thee, that I may not see my misery.
changes.candidate_text: But if Thou dost thus unto me, slay me outright, if I have found mercy with Thee, that I may not see my misery.
changes.rationale: The literary proposal uses dost for the present direct address to God, smoothing the inherited if Thou do construction while retaining the conditional request, emphatic killing and mercy clause.

changes.baseline_text: Only do not become deserters from the Lord. Do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. Their season has passed away from them, but the Lord is among us. Do not fear them.
changes.candidate_text: But do not become deserters from the Lord. Do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. Their season has passed away from them, but the Lord is among us. Do not fear them.
changes.rationale: The proposal replaces initial Only with But to express the selected adversative without adding a restriction. Deserters, food, departed season and the repeated fear prohibition remain.

changes.baseline_text: because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is upon him.
changes.candidate_text: because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is in him.
changes.rationale: Worthless treatment of the word and scattering the commandments explain emphatic destruction. The proposal retains the selected in him for the concluding sin expression instead of the inherited upon him.

changes.baseline_text: And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.
changes.candidate_text: And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.
changes.rationale: The proposal uses upon for the house, vessels and people, preserving the objects receiving sprinkling rather than placing it around them. The four contact categories remain complete.

changes.baseline_text: And the people came unto Moses and said: We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Therefore pray unto the Lord, and let Him remove the serpents from us. Moses prayed unto the Lord for the people.
changes.candidate_text: And the people came unto Moses and said: We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Therefore pray unto the Lord, and let Him remove the serpent from us. Moses prayed unto the Lord for the people.
changes.rationale: The proposal retains the selected singular the serpent in the removal petition. The surrounding plural snakes remain in verse 6; the collective force of the singular here is left available.

changes.baseline_text: He went after the Israelite man into the chamber and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her womb. The plague against the sons of Israel stopped.
changes.candidate_text: He went after the Israelite man into the kiln and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her womb. The plague against the sons of Israel stopped.
changes.rationale: Propose kiln for the selected kaminos instead of chamber. A bounded lexical inquiry found LSJ's alcove gloss but also a scholarly critique tracing its uncertain basis and arguing from the ordinary kiln sense; see lexical-checks.json. The two victims, womb and cessation of plague remain.

changes.baseline_text: and shall put of your glory upon him, that the sons of Israel may obey him.
changes.candidate_text: and shall put some of your glory upon him, that the sons of Israel may obey him.
changes.rationale: Propose some of your glory for the partitive construction, supplying natural English for the inherited put of your glory. The transfer's purpose remains Israel's obedience.

changes.baseline_text: besides the whole burnt offerings of the new moon, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, and the continual whole burnt offerings, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, according to their prescription, as a sweet savour unto the Lord.
changes.candidate_text: besides the whole burnt offerings of the new moon, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, and the continual whole burnt offering, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, according to their prescription, as a sweet savour unto the Lord.
changes.rationale: New-moon and continual offerings are additional. Propose singular continual whole burnt offering to match the selected noun, retaining the plural accompanying sacrifices and drinks.

changes.baseline_text: And the Lord was angry with me also for your sakes, saying: You shall not enter there either.
changes.candidate_text: And the Lord was angry with me also because of you, saying: You shall not enter there either.
changes.rationale: Propose because of you for for your sakes: dia with the accusative states the cause of anger, while the inherited phrase can suggest benefit. Moses remains excluded as well.

changes.baseline_text: Only the cattle we took as plunder, and the spoil of the cities we took.
changes.candidate_text: Only the livestock we took as plunder, and the spoil of the cities we took.
changes.rationale: Propose livestock for cattle: the selected generic ktene covers domestic livestock, whereas current English cattle ordinarily narrows it to bovines. The exception and city spoil remain.

changes.baseline_text: And all the cattle and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
changes.candidate_text: And all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
changes.rationale: Propose livestock for cattle to preserve the generic ktene in this plunder list. All, city spoil and for ourselves remain.

changes.baseline_text: but the seventh day is a Sabbath unto the Lord your God. You shall do no work therein, you, nor your sons, nor your daughter, nor your male slave, nor your female slave, nor your ox, nor your beast of burden, nor any of your cattle, nor the sojourner dwelling with you; that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.

You shall do no work therein, you, nor your sons, nor your daughter, nor your male slave, nor your female slave, nor your ox, nor your beast of burden, nor any of your livestock, nor the sojourner dwelling with you; that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.

changes.baseline_text: You shall burn the graven images of their gods with fire. You shall not covet the silver or gold upon them, nor take it unto yourself, lest you stumble thereby; for it is an abomination unto the Lord your God.

changes.rationale: Propose from them for upon them to represent the selected apo phrase without adding a location for the silver and gold. Burning images, rejecting gain and avoiding stumbling remain.

changes.baseline_text: For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearful God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;
changes.candidate_text: For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearsome God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;

changes.baseline_text: And He shall give grass in your fields for your cattle; and when you have eaten and are filled,
changes.candidate_text: And He shall give grass in your fields for your livestock; and when you have eaten and are filled,
changes.rationale: Propose livestock for cattle because the selected generic animal term covers the field-fed domestic animals broadly. Eating and fullness still lead into the warning.

changes.baseline_text: And you shall teach them unto your children, to speak of them when you sit in the house, and when you walk in the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
changes.candidate_text: And you shall teach your children to speak of them when they sit in the house, and when they walk in the way, and when they lie down, and when they rise up.

The accusative participles follow the children and infinitive speak, unlike the nominative parent-directed construction in 6:7. Teach your children to speak of them naturally represents the repeated word-object through one English complement.

changes.baseline_text: Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.
changes.candidate_text: Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin in you.
changes.rationale: Propose in you for upon you to preserve the selected en soi in the great-sin conclusion, alongside the inward lawless thought and evil eye. Imminent release must not motivate withholding aid.

changes.baseline_text: But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
changes.candidate_text: But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I did not command him to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.

changes.baseline_text: save the women and the dependent households. And you shall take as spoil unto yourself all the cattle, and all that is in the city, and all its goods; and you shall eat all the spoil of your enemies which the Lord your God gives you.

changes.baseline_text: and behold, he brings charges against her as a pretext, saying: I did not find the tokens of your daughter’s virginity. Yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity. And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
changes.candidate_text: and now he himself brings charges against her as a pretext, saying: I did not find the tokens of your daughter’s virginity. Yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity. And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
changes.rationale: Propose and now he himself for and behold, he. Selected autos nyn supplies personal emphasis and now, not an unexpressed behold. The allegation, counterevidence and spreading of the garment remain.

changes.baseline_text: You shall not speak peace unto them, nor seek their advantage, all your days for ever.
changes.candidate_text: You shall not speak peace unto them, nor words to their advantage, all your days for ever.
changes.rationale: Propose nor words to their advantage for nor seek their advantage: the selected speaking verb governs both peaceful and beneficial speech, without an expressed seek verb. The full duration remains.

changes.baseline_text: And if you vow a vow unto the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it; for the Lord your God shall surely require it of you, and there shall be sin upon you.
changes.candidate_text: And if you vow a vow unto the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it; for the Lord your God shall surely require it of you, and there shall be sin in you.
changes.rationale: Propose sin in you for sin upon you to retain the selected en soi. A vow must not be delayed because the Lord emphatically requires it.

changes.baseline_text: But if you do not desire to vow, there is no sin upon you.
changes.candidate_text: But if you do not desire to vow, there is no sin in you.
changes.rationale: Propose no sin in you for no sin upon you, preserving the same selected construction in the contrasting case of not choosing to vow.

changes.baseline_text: On the same day you shall pay his wages; the sun shall not go down upon them, for he is poor and sets his hope upon them; lest he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be sin upon you.
changes.candidate_text: On the same day you shall pay his wages; the sun shall not go down upon them, for he is poor and sets his hope upon them; lest he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be sin in you.
changes.rationale: Same-day payment, sunset, poverty and hope in the wages remain. En soi is rendered in you, consistent with 23:22-23, rather than upon you.

changes.baseline_text: You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.
changes.candidate_text: You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great or a small.
changes.rationale: The selected e links great or small; revise and to or while retaining differing weights as the contextual rendering of the repeated weight noun.

changes.baseline_text: You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
changes.candidate_text: You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great or a small.
changes.rationale: The corresponding measure prohibition likewise uses great or small; apply the same conjunction correction as at 25:13.

changes.baseline_text: And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.
changes.candidate_text: And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your livestock, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.
changes.rationale: The sequence is womb, land and livestock offspring. Revise generic ktenon from cattle to livestock, distinguishing it from the bovine term at 28:4.

changes.baseline_text: The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall be above, and not beneath, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day to keep and do.
changes.candidate_text: The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall then be above, and not beneath, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day to keep and do.
changes.rationale: Head versus tail and above versus beneath express the paired reversals; restore then for the selected tote in the second pair.

changes.baseline_text: And it shall consume the offspring of your cattle and the produce of your land, leaving you neither grain, nor wine, nor oil, nor the herds of your cattle, nor the flocks of your sheep, until it destroys you.
changes.candidate_text: And it shall consume the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your land, leaving you neither grain, nor wine, nor oil, nor the herds of your cattle, nor the flocks of your sheep, until it destroys you.
changes.rationale: Generic livestock offspring precede the specifically bovine herds and sheep flocks. Revise only the first cattle to livestock, leaving the later cattle for boon.

changes.baseline_text: And the Lord your God shall care greatly for you in every work of your hands, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle; for the Lord your God shall again rejoice over you for good, as He rejoiced over your fathers,
changes.candidate_text: And the Lord your God shall care greatly for you in every work of your hands, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your livestock; for the Lord your God shall again rejoice over you for good, as He rejoiced over your fathers,
changes.rationale: Care greatly preserves the selected polyoresei; generic ktenon is revised from cattle to livestock, keeping womb, land and livestock order.

changes.baseline_text: Take this book of the law, and lay it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there for a witness against you.
changes.candidate_text: Take this book of the law, and lay it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there for a witness among you.
changes.rationale: The book is beside the ark, not inside it. Revise against you to among you for en soi, leaving its adversarial function to context rather than substituting a preposition.

changes.baseline_text: Whoever disobeys you or does not heed your words in all that you command him, let him die. Only be strong and courageous!”
changes.candidate_text: Whoever disobeys you and does not heed your words in all that you command him, let him die. But be strong and courageous!”
changes.rationale: Propose and for or between disobedience and non-hearing, preserving the selected coordinating kai. Replace final Only with But for alla, which does not restrict the exhortation to strength alone.

changes.baseline_text: and keep alive my father’s household, my mother, my brothers, my whole household, and all who belong to them, and rescue my life from death.”

changes.rationale: Propose all that belongs to them for all who belong to them: the selected neuter all that they have is broader than persons alone. The repeated household groups and rescue of my life remain.

changes.rationale: Restore Behold before the hidden goods for explicit idou. The patterned carpet, two hundred silver didrachms and one fifty-didrachm gold tongue remain distinct.

changes.baseline_text: Joshua took Achar son of Zerah and brought him up to the ravine of Achor, with his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his beasts of burden, all his sheep, his tent, and everything belonging to him. All the people were with him, and he brought them up to Emek-achor.

changes.rationale: Propose calves for moschous rather than generic cattle. The shorter Achar son of Zerah, both Achor and Emek-achor, family, other animals, tent and possessions all remain.

changes.baseline_text: as Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded the sons of Israel, as written in Moses’ law: an altar of whole stones on which no iron had been applied. He offered whole burnt offerings to the Lord there and a sacrifice of well-being.

changes.baseline_text: They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Where are you from, and where have you come from?”

changes.baseline_text: When our elders and all the inhabitants of our land heard, they told us, ‘Take provisions for the journey, go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants; now make a covenant with us.”’
changes.candidate_text: When our elders and all the inhabitants of our land heard, they told us, ‘Take provisions for the journey, go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your household servants; now make a covenant with us.”’
changes.rationale: Propose household servants for the repeated oiketai self-description. Elders and all inhabitants commission the journey, provisions and covenant request.

changes.baseline_text: They were greatly afraid of them, for he knew that Gibeon was a great city, like one of the chief cities, and all its men were strong.
changes.candidate_text: They were filled with great fear, for he knew that Gibeon was a great city, like one of the chief cities, and all its men were strong.

changes.baseline_text: All who dwell in the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians, I will destroy before Israel. Only distribute it by lot to Israel, as I commanded you.

changes.rationale: Divine destruction is promised for the mountain inhabitants and Sidonians. Propose But distribute for Only distribute to preserve alla's contrast without making distribution Joshua's sole stated task.

changes.baseline_text: The boundary passes from the mountain’s summit to the spring of the water of Naphtho and passes to Mount Ephron. The boundary leads to Baal—that is the city of Jearim.
changes.candidate_text: The boundary passes from the mountain’s summit to the spring of the water of Naphtho and passes to Mount Ephron. The boundary will lead to Baal—that is the city of Jearim.
changes.rationale: The two present passage verbs are followed by future exaxei. Change leads to will lead to preserve this selected shift, retaining Naphtho, Ephron and Baal's Jearim identification.

changes.baseline_text: “Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, ‘Appoint for yourselves the cities of refuge of which I spoke to you through Moses,
changes.candidate_text: “Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, ‘Appoint the cities of refuge of which I spoke to you through Moses,
changes.rationale: The selected command is to appoint the cities of refuge previously spoken of through Moses. Remove for yourselves, which has no reflexive or beneficiary expression here; the explicit for you remains in 20:3.

changes.baseline_text: Only take great care to do the commandments and the law which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded us to do: to love the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to cling to Him, and to serve Him with all your mind and all your soul.”
changes.candidate_text: But take great care to do the commandments and the law which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded us to do: to love the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to cling to Him, and to serve Him with all your mind and all your soul.”
changes.rationale: Replace initial Only with But for alla, preserving the contrasting exhortation without an unsupported exclusive limit. The us commanded by Moses, your God, all His ways, mind and soul remain.

changes.baseline_text: If we built ourselves an altar to depart from the Lord our God, to offer on it a sacrifice of whole burnt offerings or a sacrifice of well-being, the Lord will require an account.
changes.candidate_text: If we built ourselves an altar to depart from the Lord our God, to offer on it a sacrifice of whole burnt offerings or a sacrifice of deliverance, the Lord will require an account.
changes.rationale: The conditional altar-building for apostasy and its two sacrificial purposes remain. Replace well-being with deliverance for the working rendering of the selected soteriou ritual phrase.

changes.baseline_text: We did this out of concern about this matter, saying, ‘Tomorrow your children might say to our children, “What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
changes.candidate_text: But we did this out of concern about this matter, saying, ‘It is so that your children may not say to our children tomorrow, “What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
changes.rationale: Restore initial But for alla and explicitly render hina me as so that your children may not say. Inherited might expresses fear but leaves the negative purpose implicit. The close draft preserves the elliptical purpose opening; literary It is supplies an English clause frame referring to this action, without adding a new purpose. The nested question continues into 22:25.

changes.baseline_text: but so that it may be a testimony between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform service to the Lord before Him with our offerings and our sacrifices and our sacrifices of well-being. Then your children shall not say to our children tomorrow, ‘You have no portion in the Lord.’
changes.candidate_text: but so that it may be a testimony between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform service to the Lord before Him with our offerings and our sacrifices and our sacrifices of deliverance. Then your children shall not say to our children tomorrow, ‘You have no portion in the Lord.’
changes.rationale: The altar's testimony between groups and succeeding generations concerns service before the Lord with three offering categories. Replace sacrifices of well-being with sacrifices of deliverance for the selected soterion phrase; tomorrow's denial is explicitly negated.

changes.baseline_text: May it never be that we turn away from the Lord in these present days, departing from the Lord by building an altar for offerings, salamin sacrifices, and a sacrifice of well-being apart from the Lord’s altar before His tent.”
changes.candidate_text: May it never be that we turn away from the Lord in these present days, departing from the Lord by building an altar for offerings, salamin sacrifices, and a sacrifice of deliverance apart from the Lord’s altar before His tent.”
changes.rationale: The rejection of departure, present days, repeated Lord references and separate offerings, salamin sacrifices and soteriou sacrifice remain. Change only well-being to deliverance in the last category.

changes.baseline_text: and he went out. The king’s attendants entered, saw that the upper-room doors were closed, and said, “Perhaps he is sitting on the privy in the bedroom’s retreat?”
changes.candidate_text: and he went out. The king’s attendants entered and looked, and behold, the upper-room doors were closed. They said, “Perhaps he is sitting on the privy in the bedroom’s retreat?”
changes.rationale: The repeated exit remains. Restore the explicit idou discovery with and behold after the attendants enter and look; the selected possible privy use in the bedroom retreat remains as their question.

changes.baseline_text: They waited in embarrassment, but no one opened the upper-room doors. They took the key and opened them, and there was their lord, fallen dead on the ground.
changes.candidate_text: They waited in embarrassment, and behold, no one opened the upper-room doors. They took the key and opened them, and there was their lord, fallen dead on the ground.
changes.rationale: Restore the first idou with and behold before no one opens, replacing simple but. The final there was their lord remains a natural presentative for the second idou; the fallen-dead posture and key opening are unchanged.

changes.baseline_text: And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, “Come, and I will show you the man you seek.” He entered with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the peg in his jaw.
changes.candidate_text: And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said, “Come, and I will show you the man you seek.” He went in to her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the peg in his jaw.
changes.rationale: Keep initial Behold and the final there lay as the second discovery marker. Replace entered with her with went in to her for eisēlthen pros autēn; the selected preposition does not explicitly state accompaniment. The jaw and peg remain.

changes.baseline_text: Joash said to the men who stood against him, “Do you now plead for Baal? Do you save him? Whoever disputed with him shall die by morning. If he is a god, he himself shall avenge him, for one has demolished his altar.”
changes.candidate_text: Joash said to the men who stood against him, “Do you now plead for Baal? Or do you save him? Whoever disputed with him shall die by morning. If he is a god, he himself shall avenge him, for one has demolished his altar.”
changes.rationale: Restore Or before the second question for explicit ē. Retain now, the death-by-morning statement, conditional god claim and the difficult he/him/one references without resolving them into a familiar defense speech.

changes.baseline_text: Gideon entered, and look, a man was explaining his dream to his neighbour. He said, “Look at the dream I dreamed: a cake of barley bread was rolling through Midian’s camp. It came to Midian’s tent, struck it, and overturned it, and the tent fell.”
changes.candidate_text: Gideon entered, and look, a man was explaining his dream to his neighbour. He said, “Look at the dream I dreamed: behold, a cake of barley bread was rolling through Midian’s camp. It came to Midian’s tent, struck it, and overturned it, and the tent fell.”
changes.rationale: Three idou markers frame entry, the dream introduction and the rolling barley cake. Restore the third as behold before the cake, while the first two remain look. The tent is struck, overturned and falls.

changes.baseline_text: Gideon and the hundred men with him entered a section of the camp as the middle watch began. He thoroughly roused the guards, and they sounded the horn trumpets and dashed the jars in their hands.
changes.candidate_text: Gideon and the hundred men with him entered a section of the camp as the middle watch began. But he thoroughly roused the guards, and they sounded the horn trumpets and dashed the jars in their hands.
changes.rationale: Gideon and one hundred enter at the middle watch; restore But for plēn before the emphatic singular he roused the guards. Horns and jar-dashing remain subsequent plural actions.

changes.baseline_text: And Gideon said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother.” And he swore to them, “As the Lord lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not kill you.”
changes.candidate_text: And Gideon said, “They are my brothers, the sons of my mother.” And he swore to them, “As the Lord lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not kill you.”
changes.rationale: Change They were my brothers to They are my brothers for explicit present eisin, retaining the ongoing kinship assertion. Sons of my mother, the Lord-lives oath and the unreal survival condition remain.

changes.baseline_text: He took the people, divided them into three companies, and lay in ambush there. He saw the people coming out of the city, rose against them, and struck them.
changes.candidate_text: He took the people, divided them into three companies, and lay in ambush there. He looked, and behold, the people came out of the city. He rose against them and struck them.
changes.rationale: The three-company division and ambush remain. Restore the explicit discovery marker with He looked, and behold, the people came out of the city, then separate his rising and striking into the next sentence.

changes.baseline_text: And he called quickly to the young man who bore his armour, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say, ‘A woman killed him.’” And his young man pierced him, and he died.
changes.candidate_text: And he called quickly to the young man who bore his armour, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say, ‘A woman killed him.’” And his young man pierced him, and Abimelech died.
changes.rationale: The urgent armour-bearer request preserves the feared report that a woman killed him. Restore the explicit final Abimelech died instead of he died, making clear that the death subject is not the preceding young man.

changes.baseline_text: The sons of Israel said to the Lord, “We have sinned. Do to us whatever is pleasing before Thee; only deliver us this day, O Lord.”
changes.candidate_text: The sons of Israel said to the Lord, “We have sinned. Do Thou to us whatever is pleasing before Thee; but deliver us this day, O Lord.”
changes.rationale: Propose Do Thou to represent the emphatic divine-address subject su, and but for plen, preserving the plea after unconditional submission rather than suggesting an exclusive demand.

changes.baseline_text: Gilead’s elders said to Jephthah, “May the Lord be the One who hears between us; surely we will do according to your word.”
changes.candidate_text: Gilead’s elders said to Jephthah, “The Lord shall be the One who hears between us; surely we will do according to your word.”
changes.rationale: Propose The Lord shall be for the future estai instead of May the Lord be; the elders invoke the Lord as the One hearing between them and give an oath-like assurance.

changes.baseline_text: And the men of Gilead seized beforehand the crossings of the Jordan belonging to Ephraim. And when the escaped ones of Ephraim said, “Let us cross,” the men of Gilead asked them, “Are you of Ephraim?” And if they said, “We are not,”
changes.candidate_text: And the men of Gilead seized beforehand the crossings of the Jordan belonging to Ephraim. And when the escaped ones of Ephraim said, “Let us cross,” the men of Gilead asked them, “Are you of Ephraim?” And they said, “We are not.”
changes.rationale: Propose And they said instead of And if they said: the selected text narrates a plural answer, without an explicit conditional. End the response here with a full stop.

changes.baseline_text: “Who knows whether God will relent and turn from His fierce anger, so that we certainly do not perish?”
changes.candidate_text: “Who knows whether God will relent and turn from His fierce anger, so that we shall not perish?”
changes.rationale: Propose a natural future result clause: so that we shall not perish. The displayed emphatic negative with a subjunctive expresses non-perishing, but certainly do not is awkward under the opening who-knows question and can sound like an independent present guarantee. The question remains conditional on God's possible relenting; shall not carries the firm negative without adding an assurance outside that question. His fierce anger represents the paired wrath terms. Full mood/discourse review remains open.

changes.baseline_text: The Lord said, “You spared the gourd, over which you did not toil and which you did not nurture, which came to be in a night and perished in a night.
changes.candidate_text: The Lord said, “You had pity on the gourd, over which you did not toil and which you did not nurture, which came to be in a night and perished in a night.
changes.rationale: Propose had pity on for the past form of pheidomai with the gourd as its concern. In context Jonah mourned its loss; You spared can misleadingly imply that he successfully preserved it. The same verb recurs in 4:11, where the proposed have pity on preserves that link. Middle Liddell was consulted for the general range of sparing, mercy and care; the choice here is a contextual inference, not a specialist LXX entry or apparatus verdict. The denied labor/nurture and repeated night are unchanged.

changes.baseline_text: And shall I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which dwell more than one hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right from their left, and much livestock?”
changes.candidate_text: And shall I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which dwell more than one hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right from their left, and much livestock?”
changes.rationale: Propose have pity on to match the same verb in 4:10 while retaining the divine first-person future question. Its contextual implication includes sparing the city, not merely an abstract emotion. The great-city description, more than 120,000 people, right/left ignorance and many livestock are retained. The people are not identified as infants, and the concluding question is not replaced by a doctrinal explanation. The lexical choice remains a proposal requiring review.
